proposals.evidence: Reviewed whole-form continuation of DewasDoneDanuwar sukʰla “dry” (f_uachttvc5ktdg). Family evidence: CDIAL 12548 śuṣka explicitly gives northern śukh/šuko, Hindi sūkhā and the -ll extension behind Oriya sukhilā “dry”. This supports simple sūk/sūkhī and l-extended forms; Nepali sukeko is a verbal participle requiring the underlying dry verb to be identified. Reviewed comparator: Buksa sukʰa “dry” (f_idqorou7cmcfg). Any uncertain transfer between Indo-Aryan languages remains open under the user’s preference; source phonetic details are preserved. The present source form was inspected for phonetic and gloss differences; normalization was used only to find it, and its exact spelling is preserved.

Reviewed comparison: Kal loī “blood” (f_buwn726qnc46e). Possible intra-IA borrowing remains open under the user’s policy; exact source forms are retained.
